messages.content:
You restyle the citations in an article's footnotes to match a journal's form.
Change only the form of citations: order of elements, punctuation, abbreviations, quotation marks, shortened later citations, ibid and cross-references.
Leave every sentence of discussion exactly as written. Never add information (a name, title word, place, publisher, year, page) that is not in the note itself or in an earlier note of the same article.
If a note cannot be restyled with what is given, return it unchanged. Return every note, each under its number, as plain text with no markup.

THE JOURNAL'S CONVENTIONS, as a model described them from the journal's articles:
- Citations are given in numbered endnotes or footnotes without a terminal full stop unless punctuation is present.
- Books are cited: Author, Title in Italics (Editor ed, Publisher Year) Pinpoint Page Range.
- Journal articles are cited: Author, ‘Article Title in Single Quotation Marks’ (Year) Volume Journal Name in Italics Starting Page, Pinpoint Page Range.
- Book chapters in edited collections are cited: Author, ‘Chapter Title in Single Quotation Marks’ in Editor (ed), Book Title in Italics (Publisher Year) Page Range.
- Subsequent citations use the author surname followed by a cross-reference to the first note in parentheses (eg 'Author (n 1)') followed by pinpoint page numbers.
- Immediate repetitions of the same source use 'ibid' (in lower case, unitalicised) followed by the pinpoint page number.
- Multiple citations within a single note are separated by a semicolon (eg '; see eg ').

EXAMPLE CITATIONS, copied word for word from the journal's articles:
- (book-first) Invented Author, A Made-Up Treatise (Sample Editor ed, Sample University Press 1996) 88–9.
- (book-first) Invented Author, A Made-Up Treatise (Sample Editor ed, Sample University Press 1996) 101–4.
- (book-first) Invented Author, A Made-Up Treatise (Sample Editor ed, Sample University Press 1996) 210–15.
- (book-later) Author (n 1) 201–9
- (article-first) Fictional Writer, ‘The Organisation of Liberty’ (2001) 12 Journal of Examples 123, 130–34.
- (article-later) Writer (n 3) 125–6
- (chapter-first) Another Person, ‘A Further Invented Title’ in Sample Editor (ed), A Collection of Examples (Sample University Press 2010) 310–45.
- (edited-or-translated) Invented Author, A Made-Up Treatise (Sample Editor ed, Sample University Press 1996) 88–9.
- (ibid) ibid 90.
- (ibid) ibid 127.
- (ibid) ibid 112.
- (ibid) ibid 214.
- (cross-reference) Author (n 1) 201–9; see eg Writer (n 3) 125–6.

THE ARTICLE'S FOOTNOTES, all of them, in order:
[1] Invented Author, A Made-Up Treatise, ed. Sample Editor (Exampletown: Sample University Press, 1996), pp. 88-89.
[2] Ibid., p. 90.
[3] Fictional Writer, “The Organization of Liberty,” Journal of Examples 12 (2001): 123-124.
[4] Ibid.
